summary: Midlantic Property Management, Inc. is a New Jersey community-association management firm (condos, townhomes, HOAs, high-rises, commercial and waterfront properties) with a Highland Park head office, a Long Branch office and a field office in Little Egg Harbor. It sells recurring management contracts to association boards and runs resident-facing work-order intake, after-hours emergency dispatch, mass notifications and delinquency/lien billing. Everything customer-facing is phone- or email-based on a free Weebly site last updated around 2013, and the Google profile sits at 1.6 stars, is unclaimed and lists no hours.

facts.fact: Company states it has provided full-service association management 'Since 1995', with offices in Highland Park and Long Branch and services spanning administrative management, financial/audit management, on-site services, association websites and STATCOM emergency alerts.

Head office: 315 Raritan Avenue, Highland Park, NJ 08904; phone (732) 828-7200; fax (732) 828-7238; office hours Monday-Friday 9:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m., with Friday closing at 3:00 p.m. between Memorial Day and Labor Day.

H. James Polos is President; he is a CMCA and AMS through CAI and a NJ licensed real estate broker, and the About page is signed by him. The president page says he formed the company in 1993 while the home page says 'Since 1995', and it lists a third, field office in Little Egg Harbor.

Proposal requests are accepted only by phone or by hand-written email; the page lists 11 fields the board must paste into the email (association name, address, contact, daytime phone, number of units, property type, current manager, board member status, special requirements) and there is no form on the page.

Resident work orders are submitted the same way: call (732) 828-7200 or email a template with name, street address, phones, association name, manager name and issue description; emergencies are directed to the same number.

Company says associates are on call 24/7 and that after-business-hours calls are answered by a live operator who takes facts and arranges dispatch; it also claims an in-house emergency response team (ERT).

Careers page asks candidates to fax a cover letter and resume to (732) 828-7238 and names the roles it hires: assistant manager, community manager, accounts payable, accounts receivable, staff accountant, community administrator; it says it cannot respond to every resume.
Long Branch office listed in the city's business directory as Midlantic Property Management, Inc., 640 Ocean Avenue, Second Floor Front, 732-222-1300, with web address mpm-nj.com.

The branded domain mpm-nj.com does not serve the company site: it resolves to a GoDaddy parking lander at https://mpm-nj.com/lander (checked in a browser on 2026-11-13), while the Google profile links to the free mpm-nj.weebly.com subdomain.

Google Business Profile (business 'Midlantic Property Management', 315 Raritan Ave) shows a 1.6 rating, offers 'Claim this business', 'Add hours' and 'Add missing information' prompts, and links mpm-nj.weebly.com; no hours are published.

A managed association's own site (Lighthouse Bay condos) routes residents to the Highland Park office number (732) 828-7200 for both the community manager and after-hours emergencies, and names one community manager plus an assistant.
STATCOM is a mass-notification service sold to boards that calls/emails residents' home, work and cell phones; the company says it maintains and updates resident contact information for clients.

BBB profile for the Highland Park address shows a D+ rating, not accredited, with 2 complaints in the past 3 years (one 'Order Issues' complaint from Aug 2025 marked unanswered; one 'Service or Repair Issues' complaint from Jul 2026 marked unresolved).

operations_signals: Single intake funnel: one phone number (732) 828-7200 and one general office email handle new proposals, work orders, vendor questions and emergencies, so every request starts as a phone call or a free-text email (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/submit-a-work-order.html)

Proposal intake is a manual email template with 11 fields; nothing is captured in a web form, so a board's request only becomes a record once a person retypes it (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/proposal-request.html)

Office hours are M-F 9:00-4:30 with early Friday closing in summer, so a large share of resident and board contact falls outside staffed hours and is routed to the answering service/live operator (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/contact-us.html)

After-hours coverage is a live operator plus an in-house emergency response team, i.e. dispatch decisions are made by phone with no resident self-service portal (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/emergency-procedures.html)
Billing/collections is a documented recurring workflow: assessments, 30-day delinquency, interest and late charges, lien notices and potential foreclosure (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/faqs.html)

Board meeting support is manual and recurring: notices, proxies and ballots prepared and mailed, agenda help, board packages circulated in advance, financial statements presented at meetings (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/administrative-management.html)

Work order flow covers vendor coordination and inspection scheduling across many trades - electrical, landscaping, elevators, roofs, HVAC, plumbing, boilers, pools, trash (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/property-management.html)
Company-maintained resident contact data for STATCOM notifications implies a recurring data-entry and data-hygiene workload (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/statcom.html)

Careers page still instructs fax-only resume submission, a channel most candidates no longer use, so inbound hiring interest likely goes unanswered (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/career-opportunities.html)
hiring_signals: Part-time Administrative/Accounts Receivable Assistant - HOA/Condo Property Management, Highland Park, listed at $20/hour; duties per the listing include answering calls, relaying messages, drafting correspondence, maintaining community websites and helping managers track projects, with Enumerate Central experience preferred (https://www.indeed.com/q-part-time-property-management-l-east-orange%2C-nj-jobs.html)

Company careers page names the roles it recruits for - assistant manager, community manager, accounts payable, accounts receivable, staff accountant, community administrator - which maps to a small back office carrying AP, AR, accounting and community admin together (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/career-opportunities.html)
Indeed company page shows a 3.5/5 employer rating from only 2 reviews, both from 2017, so there is no current employee-voice data (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Midlantic-Property-Management)
No open community manager or maintenance postings surfaced beyond the AR/admin role in searches run on 2026-11-13 (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Midlantic-Property-Management)
review_themes: Google rating is 1.6 stars on the business's own Maps listing, seen directly in the browser; review counts differ by source (47 on one aggregator, 63 on Birdeye, 77 on Cylex/Yably), which suggests different scrape dates rather than a single verified count (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Midlantic+Property+Management+315+Raritan+Ave+Highland+Park+NJ)

Complaint themes documented at BBB are billing/ledger disputes and service-or-repair handling: one complainant says delinquency information and late fees were not corrected and no ledger supplied, another that a repair-related charge was pursued after communication stopped; both are allegations, not findings (https://www.bbb.org/us/nj/highland-park/profile/property-management/midlantic-property-management-0221-12002517/complaints)

BBB records one unanswered complaint (Aug 2025) and rates the firm D+, not accredited - a signal that complaint handling and response discipline, not only service quality, is a weak point (https://www.bbb.org/us/nj/highland-park/profile/property-management/midlantic-property-management-0221-12002517)

No owner responses to the 1.6-star Google rating are visible on the profile, and the profile is unclaimed, so negative reviews sit unanswered in the main channel boards and residents actually read (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Midlantic+Property+Management+315+Raritan+Ave+Highland+Park+NJ)

Positive counter-signal from the company's own copy: it says many associations have stayed more than 10 years, some 18+, and staff tenures of 10-15 years, which points to sticky board relationships alongside the poor public rating (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/meet-the-president.html)

Review text elsewhere could not be retrieved: Google review bodies sit behind a limited Maps view and Yelp/Indeed/Cylex/ApartmentRatings returned 403, so specific wording could not be quoted or themed beyond the BBB descriptions (https://www.yellowpages.com/highland-park-nj/mip/midlantic-property-management-458632929)
tech_footprint: Website is a free Weebly subdomain (mpm-nj.weebly.com) on an old template build; footer reads '@2013. All Rights Reserved.' and page titles omit the town (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)

No forms anywhere: contact, proposal and work-order pages have zero form elements (verified in the DOM), and email is only exposed through Cloudflare-obfuscated links (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/contact-us.html)
Phone number is plain text - zero tel: links on the contact page - so mobile visitors cannot tap to call; the home page does not show a phone number at all (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)

No h1 on the contact page and none on the home page; no meta description; the anniversary banner ('Celebrating Its 20th Year') is an 858x67 GIF with alt text 'Picture', so that message is invisible to search engines and screen readers (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)
Header slideshow renders as an empty blank block at desktop and at 390px phone width, wasting the main visual slot (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)
Branded domain mpm-nj.com is a parked GoDaddy lander rather than the company site, so typed-in or directory traffic to the real-looking domain dead-ends (https://mpm-nj.com/lander)

A job listing references Enumerate Central as the association-management/accounting platform, the only public sign of their back-office software (https://www.indeed.com/q-part-time-property-management-l-east-orange%2C-nj-jobs.html)

Tech stack otherwise limited to Weebly hosting plus Snowplow analytics, a Facebook page (facebook.com/midlanticpropertymanagement), a LinkedIn group and a site search box; no resident portal, no online booking, no chat and no CRM widget visible (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)

The company sells client association websites (with forms, phone directory, classifieds) as a service, i.e. it builds simple static sites for boards rather than offering a SaaS portal (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/association-web-sites.html)
growth_signals: Three locations claimed over time - Highland Park HQ, Long Branch (West End) office and a Little Egg Harbor field office - suggesting a portfolio spread across Middlesex, Monmouth and Ocean counties (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/meet-the-president.html)

Client communities named in association documents returned by search include Edison Glen, Gramercy Gardens and Harbour Mansion (documents not directly opened; Lighthouse Bay's own contact page was opened and confirms the firm as manager) (https://edisonglen.org/uploads/media/Edison%20Glen%20Associates.pdf)

A 2025 Freehold Borough bill-list entry returned by search records a $44,931.80 refuse-reimbursement payment to Midlantic Property Management, evidence of active community contracts and pass-through municipal billing in 2025 (https://www.freeholdboroughnj.gov/government/meeting-documents/mayor-council-meeting/2025-mayor-council-meeting-documents/2025-agendas-mayor-council/1764-10-06-2025-mayor-and-council-agenda/file)

Hiring a part-time AR/admin assistant at $20/hour indicates the back office is capacity-constrained rather than expanding into additional community-manager roles (https://www.indeed.com/q-part-time-property-management-l-east-orange%2C-nj-jobs.html)

The most forward-looking marketing element on the site is still a 'Celebrating Its 20th Year' banner and no new service, location or award announcement appears there; the newest dated records found are the 2025-2026 BBB complaints (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)
Seasonal load is explicit: summer Friday early closure, snow-emergency notification use cases for STATCOM, and snow removal/contracting offered as a service (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/statcom.html)
physical_signals: Head office at 315 Raritan Avenue, Highland Park, NJ 08904 - a street-address office suite; no square footage or seat count is published (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/contact-us.html)
Long Branch office at 640 Ocean Avenue, Second Floor Front, 732-222-1300 (https://www.longbranch.org/DocumentCenter/View/1053/Directory-of-Businesses-in-the-City-of-Long-Branch-PDF)
Field office in Little Egg Harbor named on the president page (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/meet-the-president.html)

Property types under management stated by the company: apartment complexes, commercial properties, condominiums and townhouse communities, high-rise buildings, homeowner associations, waterfront properties (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)

Buildings and systems the firm says it inspects or schedules: elevators, roofs and rooftop decks, boilers and common-area water storage tanks, HVAC, sump pumps, pools/recreation and exercise rooms, lighting, gutters, trash removal (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/property-management.html)
24/7 emergency dispatch via live operator plus an in-house emergency response team that drills at managed sites (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/emergency-procedures.html)

On-site staffing appears selective: STATCOM notifications and the ERT are described as included in the fee for 'full-time on-site management', implying a mix of on-site and remotely managed communities (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/statcom.html)

No fleet, kitchen, health-inspection or FMCSA-style public records apply to this business type and none were found; the firm publishes no portfolio unit count or community list (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/about-mpm.html)
decision_maker: H. James Polos, President - named and signing on the company's own About page (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/about-mpm.html) and profiled on its Meet the President page (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/meet-the-president.html). The contact page offers only one general office email (address is Cloudflare-obfuscated in the page source) plus the main phone number.

inferences.inference: Headcount is small, roughly 5-20 people across three offices, with community managers supported by a shared back office.
inferences.reasoning: The careers page lists generic back-office roles (AP, AR, staff accountant, community administrator), the only current posting is part-time at $20/hour, and one phone number plus one office email serves the whole company.

inferences.inference: A material share of staff time goes to re-keying requests captured by phone and email into Enumerate Central.
inferences.reasoning: Proposal and work-order intake are email templates with 9-11 fields, there is no web form anywhere on the site, STATCOM requires the firm to maintain resident contact data, and the open job is explicitly an admin/AR assistant who relays messages and tracks projects.

inferences.inference: Reputation, not demand, is the binding constraint: the 1.6-star unclaimed Google profile and unanswered BBB complaint suppress new board inquiries more than the dated website does.
inferences.reasoning: Boards vet managers online; the profile is unclaimed, publishes no hours and shows no visible owner responses, one BBB complaint is recorded as unanswered, yet client-tenure claims run 10-18 years, so the underlying service base looks stable.

inferences.inference: The parked mpm-nj.com domain is a live risk: printed material, the Long Branch business directory and directory listings still point to it.
inferences.reasoning: The city directory lists mpm-nj.com as the company web address, that domain now serves a GoDaddy parking lander, and the Google profile instead links the Weebly subdomain - two identities for one firm.

inferences.inference: Delinquency and late-fee disputes are a recurring, rules-heavy workflow ripe for automation with a human approval step.
inferences.reasoning: The site documents 30-day delinquency, interest, late charges and lien filing, the FAQ devotes a section to non-payment, the open role is AR-focused, and both BBB complaints involve ledgers, late fees or charges.

inferences.inference: After-hours coverage is the highest-volume phone burden and the most likely place a missed call turns into a 1-star review.
inferences.reasoning: All emergencies route to one number answered by a live operator, office hours end at 4:30 p.m., and complaints cluster on communication and follow-through rather than work quality.

inferences.inference: The firm is a plausible payer for a 5-figure fix but not an early adopter.
inferences.reasoning: Recurring management fees across a multi-county portfolio plus pass-through municipal billing (a $44.9k refuse reimbursement in 2025) indicate real revenue, while a 2013-era free Weebly site, fax-based recruiting and an unclaimed Google profile indicate low technology appetite.

data_gaps: Google review bodies and the exact review count could not be read: Maps served a limited view with no review list, and google.com/search returned a bot-check page from this IP on 2026-11-13. The 1.6 rating was read directly from the Maps listing; counts (47/63/77) come from third-party aggregators and disagree.

BBB profile and complaints pages returned 403 and a 'Just a moment...' bot wall in both fetch and browser; complaint types and statuses are taken from search-engine summaries of those BBB pages, not from the page text itself.

Indeed, Yelp, Yellowpages, Cylex, ZipRecruiter and ApartmentRatings all blocked automated access (403/Cloudflare), so the $20/hour AR assistant listing, its duties and the Enumerate Central preference come from Indeed search-result summaries rather than an opened job page, and whether the role is still open is unconfirmed.

The Long Branch directory lists mpm-nj.com as the firm's web address but that domain is now a parking lander, so the company's current preferred domain cannot be confirmed from public sources; Google only shows the Weebly subdomain.
No published staff count, square footage, seat count, portfolio unit count or revenue figure was found on any accessible source.

Client-community documents (Edison Glen offering statement, Gramercy Gardens resident packet, Harbour Mansion notice) were seen only as search results; edisonglen.org failed to resolve and the other documents were not opened, so those client names are unverified.
No current (2025-2026) local news coverage, award announcements or expansion notices were found; the newest dated records are the 2025-2026 BBB complaints and a 2025 Freehold Borough bill-list entry.
The company's Facebook page and LinkedIn group could not be read (JavaScript or blocked), so posting recency and follower counts are unknown.
No fleet, kitchen, health-inspection or FMCSA-type public records apply to this business; no permit or licensing dataset was checked for the office addresses.
